SPECIAL ELECTION ISSUE HEAR FROM THE CANDIDATES ENCINO ENTERPRISE Volume 7, Issue 153 A Compendious Source of Information NEWS IN BRIEF 34th Annual Sherman Oaks Street Fair to Be Held This Sunday on Ventura Blvd. The 34th annual Sherman Oaks Street Fair returns this Sunday, October 18, from 10 am to 6 pm on Ventura Blvd., from Kester Ave. to Van Nuys Blvd. This is the largest single-day event in the Valley, with up to 100,000 attendees. There will be two entertainment stages, a cocktail lounge, a carnival, food trucks, artists, a pet zone, local business booths and more. For details, visit shermanoaksstreetfair.org. Need Clarification on the 2026 Propositions? Join the EPOA for an Interactive Discussion The Encino Property Owner’s Association will host a Zoom on Tuesday, October 20, at 7 pm with an interactive discussion of California Propositions on the General Election ballot. An easy to understand explanation of the Propositions along with pro and con arguments will be provided by a panel of distinguished public affairs consultants including Josh Englander and Yusef Robb. Don’t rely on the spin of TV commercials and mail. This is a great opportunity to hear unbiased and simplified information to become better informed before you vote. To request the Zoom link, email info@encinopoa.com. Jesse Gabriel Garners $22 Million to Clean Up Sepulveda Basin California Assemblymember and Assembly Budget Chair Jesse Gabriel was instrumental in garnering a $22 million state budget appropriate to support community improvements in the Sepulveda Basin. This transformative funding will support park accessibility, fire prevention and extreme heat mitigation, and public safety improvements. The Sepulveda Basin is over 2,000 acres and is the largest public open space in the San Fernando Valley. Gabriel will officially present a check to L.A. Mayor Karen Bass in the near future. Gabriel represents Assembly District 46, which covers from West Hills to Van Nuys. October 15,2026 Voters Urged to Walk Ballots Into Post Office or Use Local Ballot Boxes This election, voters are urged to walk their ballots into the post office, or use one of the many ballot boxes around the valley. Fears of late postmarks from reduced postal services, plus increasing mail theft, are fostering the suggestions. On their end the USPS plans to take other “extraordinary measures” for mail-in ballots. Starting October 24, 10 days before Election Day on November 3, some post offices may extend their opening and closing times by a half-hour and set up lines or drive-through lanes just for voters who want to get a manual postmark for their mail-in ballot. And starting October 26, USPS says it plans to speed up delivery of ballots. Official ballot drop boxes have arrived and are a safe, accessible means to cast your vote. Boxes are located throughout the city and will close at 8 pm on Election Day. Place your voted ballot card inside the return envelope, seal the envelope, sign and date it and drop it in the box! The boxes are bolted in place, or otherwise secured, and the ballots are picked up by teams of two people so there is no question about one person hiding ballots. Or you could vote early at a designated early voting location. You still get to vote in person, but with the number of people at the location spread out over a few days. If you love voting in person, but don’t want the line on election day, this might be an option for you. You can even keep track of your vote with a unique code that is printed on your ballot. Tracking your vote-by- mail ballot—when it is mailed, received, and counted—has never been easier. The California Secretary of State offers “Where’s My Ballot?”- a way for voters to track and receive notiﬁcations on the status of their vote-by-mail ballot. Powered by BallotTrax, “Where’s My Ballot?” lets voters know where their ballot is, and its status, every step of the way. Sign-up at WheresMyBallot.sos.ca.gov to receive automatic email, SMS (text), or voice call notiﬁcations about your ballot. Encino ballot box locations include: -Encino-Tarzana Branch Library (18231 Ventura Blvd., Tarzana) -Encino Community Center (16953 Ventura Blvd., Encino) -Balboa Sports Center (17015 Burbank Blvd., Encino) -Reseda Recreation Center (18411 Victory Blvd., Reseda) -Tarzana Recreation Center (5655 Vanalden Ave., Tarzana) Whichever option works best for you, whichever you choose, just ensure you exercise your right to vote!
Encino Enterprise, October 15, 2026, Page 6 BUSINESS Larry Thompson Candidate for United States Congress Q: The federal government gave a lot of money to California for homeless initiatives – and at one point took back $150 million that wasn’t implemented. Would you vote again for federal funding of homeless services in L.A.? A: Yes, I would vote for federal funding of homeless services in Los Angeles, with strict accountability. We have a moral responsibility to help people get off the streets and restore safe public spaces. Funding should support effective housing, mental health care, addiction treatment, and services that help people regain stability. It should come with independent audits, public reporting, firm deadlines, and measurable results. If an agency cannot put the money to work We Ask the Candidates: effectively, those funds should be redirected to providers that can. To that end, I would seek substantially greater participation from churches, synagogues, and other religious and community organizations. These groups can bring compassion, local relationships, volunteers, and experience serving people in need. I would call this partnership “Good Sam”—a Good Samaritan effort bringing government and community organizations together to help people achieve lasting stability. Participating providers would be held to the same accountability standards and expected to serve people regardless of their faith. Success must be measured by people helped into stable housing—not simply by dollars spent. Q: If you win but JOB LISTINGS: Edge Americas Sports Inc. seeks Head Coach in Los Angeles, CA. Democrats win the House, how would you make a difference as a freshman member of the minority party? A: I would make a difference by doing what I have done throughout my career as a lawyer, film producer, and talent manager: bring people together, negotiate, and deliver results. As a freshman Republican in a Democratic-controlled House, I would seek partners in both parties on practical priorities: affordability, wildfire recovery and prevention, homelessness, public safety, and bringing film and television jobs back to California. I would also build responsive district offices to help constituents navigate federal agencies, resolve problems with veterans’ benefits, Social Security, and Medicare, and pursue federal resources for our communities. Being in the minority would limit my ability to set the House agenda. It would not limit my responsibility to work hard, build relationships, and represent every constituent. My party does not decide my conscience. My job would be to put people over politics. Tracey Schroeder Candidate for CA State Assembly Q: Homeowners are fighting Assembly Bill 2011, which approves higher density in residential neighborhoods. Do you support putting apartment complexes in the middle of residential neighborhoods? A: I am OPPOSED to the unconscionable manner in which this bill became California law, removing the voice of local residents and city leaders. Sewer lines, water pressure, electricity grids, parking spaces, grocery store access and fire-escape routing have been neglected in Woodland Hills, West Hills, Encino, Tarzana, Reseda, Canoga Park, Van Nuys and throughout our state. Community voiced/ voted specific infrastructure guidelines are needed to override some of the generic defaults our state legislators dumped on the people. Some local roads were more accessible until recently; but are now squeezed-in and deemed undriveable by fire-trucks. This too must be addressed before density-housing is allowed to pour in and flood the zones. AB 2011 must be amended. We can work together and do better. Tell your friends to VOTE: Tracey Schroeder for CA State Assembly District 46. Q: There’s a provision in the “Billionaires Tax” that they can reduce the threshold to any level at will – so an average person can have their assets taxed. Do you support this provision that’s in the fine print? A: HECK NO! I believe in reducing taxes and red tape so we can make life more affordable for people. The “bait and switch” loophole in the “Billionaire tax” on the ballot would open a “Pandora’s Box” allowing astronomical tax increases on regular people, too. Vote NO. CA’s spending is nearly double what it was less than 10 years ago and we continue PAYING BILLIONS in taxes-for highly questionable notions including a non-existent train. NEW taxes are starting soon on our phones, computers, apps... gas... miles we drive... yet we are no better off. Let’s return to common sense. I’m running to help fix our school system and working to do it on a reduced state budget. California should be safe and affordable. Vote Tracey Schroeder for CA State Assembly 46 by November 3rd, 2026. Jesse Gabriel Candidate for CA State Assembly Declined to submit anwers.
